problems: The birch crown is reduced to a few slab-like leaves, while the pine resembles stacked green plates.
Asymmetry is present, but the species and torn woodland character are not convincing at stream distance.

The birch is a 4 m smooth pale #e1d3ae pole with a few short branches and a crown of small boxes (about 1.5 m) perched on top. On the board and in the vignette it reads as a lamp post or a bleached stick, not a tree.
The 'broken-top pine' is a 1.5 m brown stump topped by a flat green box slab. It has no conical or tiered pine silhouette and reads as a mushroom or a sign.
The crowns are tiny compared with the trunks, so the pair looks dead and sparse rather than wild and lush. They don't fill the street edge the way trees should.
Birch: a 4 m pale pole topped by three flat boxes (about 1.5×0.5×1 m). It reads as a T-shaped sign or a stick with a tiny hat, not a tree. The crown is far too small for the trunk.
Pine: a 3 m crooked stump with three flat green box slabs. It reads as a bonsai or bush and has no conifer silhouette (no cones or tiers).
Crown colours #7c9254 and #a8ad68 are the meadow's own base and accent colours, so both crowns melt into the grass behind them from a 40° camera.
Both trees are small relative to a 1.8 m person and the 8 m road. In the vignette the birch is the only one you notice, and only because of its white trunk.

World rule: trees: add minimum sizes so crowns read at stream scale. Street trees 5–6.5 m tall with crowns at least 2.5 m wide; wild pine 8–9 m tall. Crown masses must touch, with no floating gaps. Pines need stacked cone tiers, never flat slabs or round mushroom caps.

World rule: Foliage palette: the bible's palette gives trees the same greens as the countryside surface (#7c9254 base, #a8ad68 accent, #526b40 accent2), so every crown melts into the meadow. Add dedicated foliage colours darker and more saturated than the ground (e.g. #3e5938, #4f6b35, #66843a). Rule: tree crowns never use the countryside base or accent colours, except one small highlight.
elements.fix: Use the 24-part budget for a leaning birch with forked, unequal branches and a broken airy crown, plus a shorter pine with tapered foliage clusters concentrated heavily on one side. Push it heavily to one side (offset 1 m toward −x) so it reads as torn, and drop one mass to 3 m on a side branch. Add 3 dark #533d30 bark bands on the trunk. Add one heavy low side branch with its own small cone mass, and a shrub tussock at the base. / Birch: keep the leaning pale trunk (5.5 m) but give it a torn, lopsided crown of 5–6 irregular boxes and low cones, 3.5 m wide in total, pushed 1.2 m to one side. Use darker, more saturated greens #4f6b35 and #6e8a3a with one #a8ad68 highlight, and add 2 bare dead side-branches. Pine: make it 5 m tall with a bent trunk and 4 stacked flattened cones (#3e5938, #526b40), wide at the bottom and offset to one side (the 'heavy side'), plus a snapped bare top spike in #a58a63. Cast-shadow mass should be about 3× the current crown area.

problems: The hearth reads primarily as a tall, tidy cone of timber rather than an active communal bonfire.

The fire looks unlit. The six 2.2 m teepee logs, 0.4 m in diameter, lean in at radius about 0.47 m and form a closed wall, so the four glowing flame cones (≤1.55 m tall, centred at about 0.9 m) are completely hidden inside. From the stream camera the town's heart looks like a cold woodpile.

Grass cape: 5–6 vertical tapering strips in #a8ad68/#7c9254 hanging to mid-thigh. / Adze: a 0.7 m #76513b haft held angled forward and a 0.25×0.14×0.12 dark flint head (#5a5d57) lashed with a #e1d3ae band. Basket: a flared shape (wider cone over a cylinder), #b7976c with two darker #79563b weave bands and berries (#b5452a) visible at the top. problems: Large straight-edged hide panels read as rigid sheet material rather than stretched and weighted skins.
The entrance is visually lost among overlapping pale panels and foreground props.
A small framed square near the roof peak reads as a glass window with a white frame.
Front right: a rectangular wooden framed panel on two posts reads as a sign board or modern door frame standing on the lot.
The shelter is a jumble of overlapping flat tan slabs at mismatched angles. It reads as crumpled cardboard rather than one hide tent or pit house.
The hide shelter is 7 large rotated slabs that don't converge. Their ends cross and poke past each other, so the silhouette is a crumpled jumble of tan planes, not a hut.
There is no readable entrance from the camera. The doorway posts and the hide flap are lost against same-coloured slabs.
Poles poke out at random angles.
Hide colours (#c3a575–#d4b482) are close to the dirt ground ring, so the base merges into the plot.

World rule: avoid list: add 'flat pale planks or boards with straight edges as seats, roofs or decks', 'railings or balustrades', 'rectangular framed panels or windows', and 'smooth egg-shaped ellipsoid stones; use angular faceted boulders'.
elements.fix: Preserve the shelter footprint but introduce sagging panel edges, uneven seams, visible lashings and weighted corners. Frame one unmistakable dark entrance large enough for a 1.8 m resident, and move props clear of its approach. / Remove the framed square and replace it with an open smoke hole (a dark #533d30 ring at the apex with 3 pole tips poking out). Remove the framed panel. If an entrance is needed, use a rolled-up hide flap (cylinder #c3a575) over a dark doorway gap. Consolidate the shelter into one readable hide cone or dome (about 5 m dia, 4 m tall) made of 6–8 hide panels in alternating #c3a575/#987052, with visible lashing seams and 1 lean-to annex. Keep the hearth, log and owner post. / Build a single clear conical tent: one large cone (5 m diameter, 4.5 m tall, #b68b59) with 2–3 overlapping hide patch boxes laid on its surface in #8b6a50 and #c3a575. Add 6 pole tips that converge and stick 0.8 m out of the apex, and a dark #3b2a22 triangular doorway (1 m wide, 1.6 m tall) facing +z with a pale flap folded back. Keep the stone ring, fire pit and drying rack. Darken the yard ring to #79563b so the tent sits on it with contrast.

problems: The regular rectangular canopy and straight serving shelf read as a contemporary stall translated into tan materials.
The repeated roof panels lack the sag, irregular perimeter and lashings needed to identify stretched hide.
The roof is a flat rectangular slab of pale sawn planks with straight seams and square corners, on four straight posts. It reads as a modern pergola or market gazebo.
The long serving log has bowls lined up in a perfectly regular row, like a café counter.

The roof is three flat, nearly horizontal rectangular panels on straight ridge beams and 4 vertical posts. It reads as a modern pergola or carport, the 'modern furniture covered in fur' trap from the avoid list.
The pale rafter ties are evenly spaced like engineered slats.
The large green ellipsoid at the right edge reads as a giant bush or a slime blob.
There is no broth pot. The fire is under a small tripod, but nothing says 'serving warm broth'.

World rule: avoid list: add 'flat pale planks or boards with straight edges as seats, roofs or decks', 'railings or balustrades', 'rectangular framed panels or windows', and 'smooth egg-shaped ellipsoid stones; use angular faceted boulders'.
elements.fix: Rework the shelter around crooked forked poles and an asymmetrically tensioned hide canopy with visible ties. Replace the precise serving shelf with a rough split-log bowl rest or ground spread, and make a broth vessel beside the embers the functional focus. Retain simple log seating and an open entrance. / Replace the flat plank roof with a sagging sloped hide-and-bark roof: 3–4 overlapping irregular panels (#c3a575, #987052) tilted 15–20°, with ragged overhanging edges and 2 hide strips hanging. Make the posts crooked (±8°) with forked tops holding a ridge branch. Scatter the bowls irregularly (5, different sizes) and add a clay pot on hearth stones over the fire. / Make the shelter a sagging lean-to: tilt the hide roof 0.45 rad, low at the back (1.4 m) and high at the front (2.8 m). Use 3 hide panels of different sizes with a visible sag (a middle panel 0.15 m lower) on crooked posts of different heights, and remove the evenly spaced slats. Hang a big dark clay pot (0.7 m, #533d30, with an orange #f07835 glow rim of broth) from the tripod over the fire. Line up 3–4 pale bowls on the log counter. Replace the green blob with a stack of firewood.

problems: The noisy meadow, coin-like moss pattern and dense square mottling compete with the small residents and props.
Continuous straight green margins recreate the visual organisation of sidewalks despite using vegetation materials.
The central hearth lacks a strong warm focal point, while pale seating and small ownership details disappear into the ground.
elements.fix: Unify terrain with larger, lower-contrast patches and irregular transitions while preserving the town grid and parcel footprints. Break the continuous walking-edge bands, strengthen the bonfire's low warm silhouette and give important markers clean local contrast. Recheck at actual stream size with 1.8 m residents, then validate part budgets, dimensions and glow flags in the source.

problems: The right idea (crooked sticks and an empty twig loop, no sign board), but the loop is only about 2.8 m tall and about 1.6 m wide, built from dark-brown sticks on dark mottled ground. In the vignette it is a barely visible speck and doesn't read as 'available' from stream distance.
The 'mud thickened with pale ochre' isn't visible. The loop is uniformly brown, and the only pale ochre is two tiny 0.3 m dabs.
There is almost no ground clutter: one grey stone and one tuft cone.
The twig loop is brown (#76513b/#987052) standing on brown-green moss next to brown mud. It has almost no value contrast and is a small speck in the bottom corner of its cell.
The 'pale ochre' daub the bible asks for is only two 0.3 m spheres, which are invisible at cell scale.
The loop is about 1.8 m across, too small to carry the 'vacant / available' meaning from the stream camera.
There is no ground clutter apart from one grey stone and one tuft.
World rule: Part counts in the bible (street 14, lot-sale 10, market 20) disagree with the specs (28, 20, 40). Either loosen them to ranges or the designer will keep drifting.

World rule: lotRough surface: the moss pattern's high-contrast olive/brown blotches are loud enough to swallow anything brown placed on it (the free-lot loop, civic marker). Lower its contrast (accent and accent2 within about 10% value of base) or switch to plain trampled grass so lot markers can read.

World rule: lotMarkers: require the free-lot loop to be at least 2.4 m across and daubed mostly in pale clay (#e1d3ae/#c3a575), with brown only on the uprights. A brown loop on moss is invisible. Replace the civic-lot 'four corner stones' with angular ochre-banded standing slabs (the smooth ellipsoids read as eggs), and require a large pale disc with dark marks on the civic post.
elements.fix: Scale the marker up about 1.4× (loop outer about 2.2 m wide, top at about 3.4 m). Recolour 4 of the 8 loop segments in pale ochre mud #c3a575/#e1d3ae so the ring contrasts against the moss lot. Add a 0.8 m pale ochre mud-daubed collar where the two posts meet the ground. Add 2 more stones and 2 tussocks around its base. Keep the centre clearly empty. / Enlarge the loop to 2.6 m outer diameter on two 1.4 m crooked uprights. Thicken the loop segments to 0.3 m. Daub the whole loop in pale clay: alternate segments #e1d3ae and #c3a575, with brown only on the two uprights, so it reads as a bright empty ring against the moss. Add a 1.6 m ring of 6 pale stones (#a4a18d) on the ground under the loop, and 2–3 darker #526b40 tussocks nearby. Never fill the centre.

problems: Reads as a torch, which is good, but the stake is a perfectly straight vertical dark cylinder and at board scale it looks like a matchstick.
The fork, hide bindings and resin bark bundle the bible asks for aren't distinguishable. The 'cairn' at its base is two pebbles.
The flame is small (about 0.4 m) and only a sliver shows from the 40° camera.
It reads as a torch, but the stake is two perfectly square straight boxes stacked, which looks machine-cut rather than like a crooked branch.
The flame cluster is about 0.6 m wide at 2.8 m height. On the stream it reads as a small orange dot; it is fine close up but under-sized next to the 8 m road.
elements.fix: Lean the stake 6–8° and add a visible fork at about 2.0 m (two cylinders 0.1 dia, 0.5 m long, splaying 30°). Seat a bark bundle (cylinder 0.35 dia × 0.5 m, #987052) in the fork with two cream #e1d3ae binding rings. Use 3 glow flame cones (0.55, 0.4, 0.3 m wide; 0.7–0.9 m tall; #f07835/#e9b04c) leaning slightly. Build the base cairn from 4–5 stones up to 0.4 m. / Replace the box stake with two slightly tilted cylinders (0.22 and 0.18 m) offset by 0.1 m so it reads crooked. Add a fork at the top. Scale the flame cones by 1.4× (about 0.85 m wide, 1.3 m tall) with a #ffd075 inner core. Wrap the bark bundle with a pale #e1d3ae binding band so the head of the torch has contrast against the dark wood.

problems: The marker is an orange disc with pale dots on a stick. It reads as a lollipop, a flower or a cookie sign, a symmetrical 'lollipop' shape on the very lot that's supposed to say 'build together'.
The four corner stones are smooth egg ellipsoids standing upright, which read as eggs.
At 2.9 m the marker is small, and from stream scale it is visually confusable with a street tree.
The four corner stones are smooth pale ellipsoids (0.8×1.3 m) that read as giant eggs.
The forked-stick marker with a round tan disc and four white dots reads as a lollipop or a flower, and is small; the 'shared centre' meaning does not come across.
On the busy moss-camo ground, the plot looks almost identical to the free lot, apart from the eggs.

elements.fix: Replace the disc with a flat irregular clay slab (box 1.1×0.8×0.12 m, #b58b58, rotated 6°) lashed into a tall forked stick (2.2 m, 2 crooked prongs). Press 4 cream #e1d3ae hand-print dents around a shared central charcoal #533d30 circle on it. Replace each egg corner stone with an angular boulder of 2 overlapping rotated boxes (#81847a/#a4a18d, about 0.9 m tall) and a small ochre mark on each. / Replace the corner eggs with angular standing stones (rotated boxes 0.5×1.4×0.4, two greys) each banded with an ochre #c88343 stripe. Press four dark #533d30 hand marks pointing to a central #e9b04c dot, so it is a bold pale disc with dark marks rather than a tan disc with pale dots. Add a faint ring of 8 small pale stones (radius 3 m) around the project centre to say 'shared ground' without filling it.

problems: The mantle is a near-white cream block, not a broad layered hide. The figure reads as wearing a white tunic.
The headdress is mostly a fan of orange, red and yellow spikes that reads like a flame or a war-bonnet stereotype. The antlers are thin pale stubs that barely read.
The ochre face marks aren't visible at stream scale.

The headdress is four small cones 0.22 m wide and about 0.75 m tall clustered together, plus pale antler tines. At game scale it reads as a small tuft, not an 'asymmetric antler-and-feather headdress' of office.
The mantle is #e1d3ae/#f3e8cb, the same near-white as the residents' clothing. The Chief does not stand apart from townsfolk by colour.
The staff is a thin dark 0.14 m pole whose bone top is small. Ochre face marks are invisible.
There is a flat 2.3 m tan disc (#aa8257) under the figure that reads as a stray platform.
World rule: head: add 'antlers are the dominant headdress element; at most 2 feathers, no feather fan or war bonnet', to avoid a stereotyped silhouette and keep the office readable.

World rule: head: the Chief's mantle should not share the residents' near-white clothing colours. Specify a dark fur mantle with a bright collar, and a headdress at least 1 m wide and 0.9 m tall, so office reads by silhouette and value at stream scale.
elements.fix: Mantle: 2 stacked layers, the upper a fur collar wider than the shoulders (0.7 m) in #76513b and the lower a hide cape to the knees in #987052, with an irregular hem. Headdress: make the antlers the hero, 2 branched antlers (each a main beam with 2 tines, #e1d3ae, 0.6 m tall) set asymmetrically with one higher. Cut the feathers to 2 dark #533d30/#e9b04c feathers on one side only. Add 2 bold ochre #c88343 stripes across the face box (0.34×0.05 m each). / Make the headdress about 1.1 m wide and 0.9 m tall above the head: two asymmetric pale antlers (one 0.7 m with 3 tines, one shorter and broken) plus 5 fanned feathers 0.25 m wide in #d9534f-free strong colours #f07835, #e9b04c and #3b2a22. Mantle: a dark fur #533d30 cape to the knees with a bold pale #e1d3ae collar ring, so the silhouette is dark with a bright crown. Staff: 0.2 m thick, 2.4 m, topped with a 0.5 m skull or bone knot. Add 2 bold ochre #c88343 face stripes 0.06 m tall. Remove the base disc.

problems: Pale grey blocks on both sides of the head read like headphones or earmuffs, a direct anachronism.
The 'patchwork fur wrap' isn't visible. The figure is dark trousers and torso with an orange strip, like a modern hiker with a backpack.
The hooked staff has a square right-angle hook that reads as a cane or a gallows.
The hood and body are dark (#574337/#3b2a22), and the hood swallows the head into a dark ball. From the stream camera it is a dark figure with a pale stick.
The hide bundle on the back is a cylinder with a flat top that reads as a barrel or a drum.
The 'from far away' cue (pale shell beads) is a few tiny spheres that won't read.
elements.fix: Remove the grey head-side blocks. Make the hood a fur cowl that drapes from the head onto the shoulders (box 0.5×0.3×0.4, #5a3a28). Wrap the body to the knees in 3 patch panels (#76513b, #987052, #c3a575) with a braided #533d30 belt. Staff: a crooked 2 m shaft with a curved hook made of 3 angled cylinders (not a square box), with a small hide tassel. Keep the shell beads and add a hide bundle with a painted unfamiliar emblem (#4d9495 spiral). / Lighten the patchwork wrap: alternate #a87846, #c88343 and #533d30 patches as 3–4 offset boxes. Pull the hood back to show the face. Make the back bundle a rounded hide roll (horizontal sphere/cylinder 0.9 m) tied with a #e1d3ae cord, with a large 0.3 m painted foreign emblem disc in #4d9495 on it. Make the shell necklace 6 larger 0.1 m pale beads hanging in a visible arc.

problems: The tiered wooden platforms carry straight, even railings and flat deck boards. They read as modern balconies or decking.
The rock mass is a smooth rounded grey cone. It reads as a bell or a mound of putty, not a faceted cliff.
Each level looks like a cabin with a flat roof and door frame rather than a cave mouth with a hide flap.

World rule: avoid list: add 'flat pale planks or boards with straight edges as seats, roofs or decks', 'railings or balustrades', 'rectangular framed panels or windows', and 'smooth egg-shaped ellipsoid stones; use angular faceted boulders'.
elements.fix: Remove the railings and use lashed branch guards (2–3 crooked cylinders at different heights per ledge). Build the rock from 8–10 rotated angular boxes in #81847a/#a4a18d/#6f6e66 with ochre handprints on 2 faces. Turn each level's doorway into a dark cave mouth with a rolled hide flap, and replace flat cabin roofs with leaning bark lean-tos. Keep the ladders but make them notched single logs or 2-pole ladders with uneven rungs.

problems: The age translation is right (a lashed hauling sledge), but nothing pulls it. A sledge 'driving round the blocks' by itself reads as magic or a broken animation.
The pale rectangular harness loop at the front is lying flat and reads as a rope picture frame.
The red rectangular flag reads as a modern pennant.
Seen alone, the sledge reads as a log raft: the runners are straight logs with no upturned fronts.
The pale harness loop at the front reads as a picture frame lying on the ground.
Bundles and lashings are all cream and tan, so the cargo merges into the sledge.
World rule: designDirection: 'a car becomes a lashed hauling sledge' must name its puller (a wolf-dog pair or a hauling person). A moving sledge with no puller reads as broken.
elements.fix: Add a puller: either a pair of wolf-dogs (reuse the dog proportions, 0.9 m long) in hide harness, or a hauling figure leaning forward with a tumpline. Connect it with 2 cord lines (thin boxes 0.06 m) to the sledge's front. Raise the harness loop to chest height of the puller. Replace the flag with a ragged hide strip with an owner-red #d9534f stripe tied to a crooked pole. / Curve the runner fronts up: add a 0.6 m upturned box segment at the front of each runner, rotated about 0.6 rad. Replace the flat pale loop with two dark #533d30 drag poles that rise to 0.8 m at the front, joined by a cross-bar. Recolour one cargo bundle dark #533d30 and one ochre #c88343 so the load reads. Keep the red pennant.
